segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, so quick deal desk review before the 2:00. I cleaned up the DeltaForge renewal in the CRM, 84 seats, same support tier, and the pricing sheet has it at $18,900 for the year.

segments.speaker: Chris
segments.text: Good. Did you fix the invoice contact? Last time billing had accounts payable and the controller both getting copies.

segments.text: Yep, billing tool is updated to ap@deltaforge.com only, net 30, PO number 44718. Nothing weird there.

segments.text: Okay. What else is on fire?

segments.text: Northlake is the one I'm worried about. Their agreement ended July 31, and today is August 6. We have not talked to them about carrying on, at all. segments.text: Yeah, not great. Let's not touch pricing until we know if they even have budget approved. Who owns the relationship day to day?

segments.text: Jenna on customer success. I can ask her for context, but I'll send the customer note myself so it's not three people jumping in.

segments.text: Keep it simple. Ask for a 20-minute call this week, reference current usage, and say we want to align on next steps. Don't mention internal timing.

segments.text: Agreed. Also, their last invoice was $7,560 quarterly, paid on July 12, no balance due. So finance won't be the blocker.

segments.speaker: Chris
segments.text: Okay. For the 2:00, bring DeltaForge and Northlake, leave the small trial conversions out unless someone asks.

segments.text: Will do. I'll update the CRM notes after I send the email, and I'll flag you if they push back on term length.
